name: Saint Patrick
history: A Briton taken as a slave to Ireland at sixteen, who escaped, became a priest and went back to the people who had enslaved him. As bishop he preached through much of Ireland, baptised thousands and ordained clergy. His own Confession, written in plain, humble Latin, tells his story. He is the patron of Ireland.
life: Patrick was born in Roman Britain, the son of a deacon, Calpurnius, and grandson of a priest. He tells us that he did not know the true God when Irish raiders carried him off. For six years he herded animals, and in hunger and cold he began to pray, up to a hundred times a day and as often at night. A voice in a dream told him a ship was ready, and he walked some two hundred miles to find it. Home again, he dreamed of a man bringing letters, ‘the voice of the Irish’, begging him to come and walk among them once more. He was trained and ordained, and returned as a bishop. In his Letter to Coroticus he condemned a British chieftain whose men had killed and enslaved newly baptised converts. The shamrock and the banished snakes are later legend; the Confession shows a man astonished at God’s mercy.
prayerTo: Saint Patrick, you forgave those who enslaved you and brought them the faith. Pray for Ireland and her people throughout the world, for all held in slavery today, and for me, that Christ may be before me, behind me and within me, and that I may never be ashamed of Him. Amen.
prayer: Christ be with me, Christ within me, Christ behind me, Christ before me, Christ beside me, Christ to win me, Christ to comfort and restore me. Christ beneath me, Christ above me, Christ in quiet, Christ in danger, Christ in hearts of all that love me, Christ in mouth of friend and stranger.
prayerSource: Saint Patrick’s Breastplate, tr. Cecil Frances Alexander, 1889
penance: Patrick was himself a slave. Give today to a charity that works against human trafficking, and pray the Breastplate for someone held against their will.
meditation: I, Patrick, a sinner, the most unlearned of men, so his Confession begins. He knew he had been found by mercy. Can you begin your own story the same way?
